observation_summary: The application throws a StackOverflowError during generic type resolution when encountering a self-referential generic type definition (e.g., T extends GenericsSelfReference<T>).
hypothesis: The recursive resolution logic in GenericMetadataSupport enters an infinite loop because it fails to check if the type parameter being processed is identical to the actual type argument, leading to redundant processing of the same type.
prediction: Adding a guard condition to check if 'typeParameter != actualTypeArgument' before adding it to the map will break the infinite recursion.
experiment_rationale: The fix diff shows the addition of an 'else if (typeParameter != actualTypeArgument)' condition to the existing logic, which directly prevents the recursive loop identified in the stack trace.
reasoning_summary: The bug is caused by a missing guard condition in a recursive method. The fix adds a conditional check to prevent the infinite recursion, which is the definition of a 'Checking' defect in ODC.
evidence_used: Stack trace shows infinite recursion in GenericMetadataSupport.getActualTypeArgumentFor

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the recursion is part of the algorithm, the root cause is the missing guard condition to terminate the recursion, which is specifically categorized as 'Checking'.
